newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up on speculative bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up on speculative bargain hunting.

text.p: Thai stocks finished slightly higher on Friday on late bargain hunting by speculators on the eve of a deadline for Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa to quit his job, brokers said.
The SET index gained 5.15 points to 1,047.95 on moderate 3.9 billion baht turnover. Gainers led losers 191 to 92 with 137 ending unchanged. The SET-50 index rose 0.38 point to 80.02.
"The market was depressed by continued political uncertainty. Nobody knows who will succeed Banharn or if he would dissolve parliament," said Lan Pajasalmi of First Asia Securities.

The market has been sluggish since Banharn announced last Saturday that he would quit in seven days, apparently in exchange for support from coalition partners to help him win a no-confidence vote in parliament.
The index rallied about 40 minutes before closing as bargain hunters bought selected energy and commerce stocks.
Securities One topped the active list, adding three baht to 181, Bangkok Bank gained two to 220, and Dhana Siam rose one to 106.
Major losers on Friday included PCM Precast Floors, retreating four baht to 36.75, and Thai Sreshtharkich, shedding 6.50 to 61.50.
Brokers said the market is expected to move in a narrow 1,040-1,050 range on Monday.
